title: Extension by zero base change
statement:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of
schemes and a Cartesian
square with base change $a:Z'\to Z$, extension by zero
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) is exact and

$$
a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!a_U^{-1}F
$$

for every sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$, and the same holds for complexes.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.70.5, [Tag `03S6`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6).*)

proof.text: The exactness clause is the étale extension-by-zero exactness theorem: for every short exact sequence of sheaves on $U_{\Et}$, applying $j_!$ gives a short exact sequence on $Z_{\Et}$. Applying the functor degreewise therefore preserves complexes, quasi-isomorphisms, and acyclic complexes.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] with $Y=Z\prime$, $X=Z$, $f=a$, $V=U$, and $j$ the given open immersion; then $V\prime=U\prime$ and $f\prime=a_U$. Specializing its commutative coefficient ring to $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ gives the abelian-sheaf base-change morphism $j\prime_!a_U^{-1}F\to a^{-1}j_!F$ as an isomorphism. Inverting it gives the displayed direction $a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j\prime_!a_U^{-1}F$. The cited theorem identifies this map as the canonical mate, so this is the requested canonical comparison rather than merely an abstract isomorphism.

Write b_F for the canonical natural sheaf isomorphism of Step 2. For a complex K, define b_K^n=b_{K^n}. Naturality for d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1} gives j′_!a_U^{-1}(d^n) \circ b_{K^n}=b_{K^{n+1}} \circ a^{-1}j_!(d^n), so these components form a chain map. Multiplying this equation by the component inverses gives a chain map in the reverse direction. Their composites are the identity in every degree, proving the isomorphism of complexes. The complex clause here is the degreewise application of extension by zero specified in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]; it requires no boundedness and makes no identification with pro-etale, adic, or rational coefficient categories.

blueprint_update.statement:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ of
schemes and a Cartesian
square with base change $a:Z'\to Z$, extension by zero
([def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]) is exact and

$$
a^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!a_U^{-1}F
$$

for every sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$, and the same holds for complexes.

proof.text:
Extension by zero is computed sectionwise as in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]: for etale $V\to Z'$ the sections
of $j'_!a_U^{-1}F$ over $V$ are the sections of $a_U^{-1}F$ over
$V\times_{Z'}U'$, i.e. over $V\times_ZU$, while
$(a^{-1}j_!F)(V)=j_!F(V\times_ZZ_V)$ has the same description; the
Cartesian identification gives the natural isomorphism, and for
complexes the same argument applies termwise.
